newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - March 4.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - March 4.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In the opening address for Yates Property Corporation Pty Ltd, which is suing several legal advisers for A$8.5 million plus interest since 1985, David Quick QC told the court the legal advisers to YPC -- a land owner at the Darling Harbour site in Sydney -- failed to claim Ian Yates's property had special value when it was resumed and so did not get the right price. Page 2.

A report from the Corporations Law Simplification Task Force has recommended that fundraisings, takeovers and other securities dealings be exempt from section 52 of the Trade Practices Act, which deals with misleading or deceptive conduct, and should be overturned by the Corporations Law. Page 4.

Conservative accounting policies at Sydney Harbour Casino Holdings, which has been boosted in recent months by Kerry Packer's move to buy the management contract, have slashed the casino's results, leaving it with a net profit of just A$900,000 for its first full year of operation. Page 19.

Crown Ltd chairman Lloyd Williams has suggested that some analysts miscalculated Crown's revenue streams, saying it had outperformed its prospectus forecasts in its first year and revenue would be bigger when the permanent casino was opened in late April beause it would double the size of the temporary casino. Page 19.

Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation has revealed it, along with its joint venture partner Softbank, is planning to sell of off SOFTBANK/News Corp Media Co, a 50:50 venture that last year bought 21.4 per cent of the TV Asahi network, as part of a move to withdraw from the Japanese free-to-air broadcasting market. Page 19.

Oil Search Ltd managing director Peter Botten told an analysts' briefing yesterday that he predicted Papua New Guinea's Moran oil field would prove substantially larger than the nearby 305 million barrel Kutubu oil fields, and would cost far less to develop. Moran is set for its first oil production in the September quarter after being discovered last year. Page 21.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Amid speculation that the next monetary move by the Reserve Bank of Australia could be a tightening, more than A$4.3 billion was wiped off the value of the share market yesterday as investors grappled with the prospect of interest rates being left on holdand on a rise in the United States. Page 19.

Bougainville Copper Ltd shares rose two cents yesterday to 58 cents after RTZ-CRA informed the market and shareholders it expected a formal offer from the Papua New Guinea Government for its 53.6 per cent stake in the company, which controls the dormant Panguna open-pit copper mine. Page 19.

Sydney Harbour Casino announced a A$900,000 net profit for the 1996 calendar year after massive abnormal costs reduced a A$73.7 million operating profit for the period. The losses reflect the casino's conservative approach to writing off pre-opening, pre-rental interest and debt costs associated with its temporary and permanent casinos, with executives predicting steady gains in earnings and attendances at its temporary facility. Page 19.

Visy Industries confirmed yesterday the resignations of senior executives John Wheeler and Stephen Webster during the past week. It is understood Wheeler was recently promoted within the group, but the departures coincides with a tough operating period inthe paper and packaging group for Visy and its main competitor Amcor Ltd. Page 19

Gardening products group Arthur Yates and Co Ltd reported yesterday a seven per cent drop in first-half earnings with a net profit of A$4.2 million to December 31 against A$4.51 million in the previous corresponding period. Sales dipped 3.5 percent to A$8.4 million with Yates still paying a fully franked interim dividend of two cents a share. The group is confident internal efficiencies and an upturn in the retail sector will deliver an improved performance this year. Page 21.

Crown Ltd chairman Lloyd Williams said Prime Minister John Howard's concerns about the growth of gambling were "irrelevant". Williams said he was unconcerned by suggestions of a legislative cap on gambling, his comments coming after Crown Ltd shareholders approved a deal to allow Crown's major shareholder, Hudson Conway Ltd, to exercise Crown options now rather than in 1999. Page 21.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

In a result which is in line with stockbroking analysts' expectations, Sydney Harbour Casino yesterday reported an annual net profit of A$900,000 after booking a A$70.3 million in abnormal losses associated with the planned December opening of its permanet casino. Operating profit before abnormals and tax totalled A$73.7 million, struck on revenue of A$375.4 million. Page 25.

It is believed close to 40 per cent of staff, or 700 jobs, will today be cut from ANZ finance company subsidiary Esanda. ANZ remained silent on details of the plan yesterday, but the bank's head of media relations, David Wilson, said that if job losses occurred in any part of the bank, management would try to deploy those affected to other parts of the organisation. Page 25.

According to a confidential Telstra source, Telstra staff were advised last Thursday that they are now banned from sending e-mail messages direct to Telstra chief executive officer Frank Blount. The move was in response to an increasingly angry flood of email that has been sent to Blount in the past few months from Telstra's remaining 65,000 employees. Page 25.

Continuing his positive assessment of Australia's economy yesterday, Federal Treasurer Peter Costello said promising signs have emerged that economic growth is about to take off, saying Australian Bureau of Statistics figures show higher exports, bigger iports of capital equipment and positive trends in the housing industry. Page 25.

Diversified services provider Spotless Group reported yesterday a 33 per cent drop in interim net profit, with an after-tax profit of A$8.3 million to December 31 which included a A$5.57 million abnormal profit. Sales revenue of A$350 million fell beneathrecent growth trends, with the group saying it remained reasonably optimistic about business growth through new opportunities. Page 30.

Niugini Mining has reported a total loss of A$49.78 million for the December year compared with a A$5.02 million profit in 1995. US$14.6 million was lost from the group's goldmines and exploration activities for the year with asset writedowns and abnormallosses of US$24.3 million. Page 30.
THE AGE

ANZ Bank head of media relations David Wilson says changes at its Esanda finance company subsidiary today would be the forerunner to further developments over the next few months. It is believed about 700 jobs will be cut from Esanda, but the bank remaine silent on the details yesterday. Page B1.

Thanks to a rise in visitor numbers and stronger-than-expected returns from gaming machines, Sydney Harbour Casino has overcome huge abnormal losses associated with the planned December opening of its permanent casino to post an annual net profit of A$900,000. Page B1.

The Australian Securities Commission has issued a package of reforms, consisting of nine policy statements resulting from two-and-a-half years of industry and consumer consultation, for the investment advisory industry. The ASC believes the package, whichwill affect 24,000 advisers, will change the way people deal with their investment advisers. Page B1.

Crown shareholders yesterday approved a deal allowing its biggest shareholder Hudson Conway to lift its stake from 30.9 percent to 39.1 percent. Several shareholders protested over the discounting of the options price, with HudCon asked to pay only A$1.03 compared to the original price of A$1.15 per option. Page B1.

New South Wales-based gas distributor AGL is offering electricity to big NSW electricity users aided by Victorian electricity distributor Solaris, which it half-owns. AGL is positioning itself as a company that can take the complexity out of negotiations Over electricity supply, with a spokesman saying the company had "some customers" but could not name any yet. Page B3.

Listed technology group Keycorp reported yesterday a rise in net profit to A$180,000 for the December half, up from A$115,000 in the previous first half. Managing director John Wood said it would be an attractive takeover target as its importance in bankig was recognised, but Keycorp's good relationship with its major shareholders would help its defence. Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373 1800
